mechanisms.title: Mirrored-glyph back-print ownership
mechanisms.what: Compare weak bands with a local atlas of normal glyph shapes, testing direct and reflected matches plus nearby independent supporting rows.
mechanisms.data_contract_current: Gray, boxes, optional requested regions -> tones, atlas glyph arrays, per-region front/back/unknown states and suppress indices.
mechanisms.principles: Mirrored recurrence is more specific than faintness and appropriately preserves unknowns. It is still a component-shape proxy, not character recognition, and short running heads may lack enough corroboration.
mechanisms.constants_and_units: Weak nomination uses tone < .72 of the page high tone, core < .5 anchor core, width >2h; up to 12 anchors (6 sampled), >=3 anchors and high>.08; two nearby supporters can corroborate a weak band.
mechanisms.rendering_evidence: FEATURES_B records explicit/direct/reflected glyph renderings and controls. Current approved back-print removals survive exactly; short faint pieces remain.
mechanisms.special_cases: No page/book identifier enters this mechanism. Thresholds and version branches are nevertheless cohort-developed, not independently calibrated.
mechanisms.vetoes_and_duplication: Type recovery carries an older near-copy with the same shape matching. Main path has 180 suspects/39 pages but 61 removals on only 3; not an adequate substitute for final faintness.

alternatives.gain_loss: Use the shared component atlas and row-aligned reflection evidence only for ambiguous weak runs: retains causal specificity, avoids a second full box census, still cannot prove all show-through.
Deleting removes 61 currently suppressed source bands unless final faintness independently covers them; no ablation establishes that coverage.

mechanisms.verdict_reason: Retain mirror evidence as an optional ink witness; remove the type-prefixed copies and reuse a single measured context.

rust.numerical_sensitivity: 8-bit percentile interpolation, glyph normalization/resize and best-match ties matter. Do not rename a reflected score as a probability.
